producer.nose: Roasted nuts lead into orange zest, vanilla, coffee and molasses.
producer.finish: Gentle spice, fruit and restrained oak linger with a creamy character.
producer.summary: A blend of pot-distilled and column-distilled Jamaican rums, each matured for at least 15 years.

critics.nose: Very ripe tropical fruit, custard, honeyed cake, coconut, raisins and leather.
critics.palate: The aromatic fruit and dessert character continues, joined by cooked cherries, chocolate, coffee, nuts, tobacco and tea.
critics.finish: Moderately long and gently tingling, with layered fruit, roasted flavors and baking spice.
critics.summary: A dry, medium-bodied aged rum particularly suited to drinkers who enjoy pronounced Jamaican fermentation character.

notes: Producer does not separate palate notes or specify cask construction. Critic explicitly identifies the 15-year expression at 43%.

producer.summary: The brand describes X.A as smooth and balanced, combining reposado, añejo and extra-añejo components without additives.

critics.nose: Grapefruit, lime and tangerine peel accompany roasted agave and grassy nuances.
critics.palate: Medium-bodied roasted agave with sweet spice, rosemary and a suggestion of pineapple skin.
critics.finish: Sweetness is counterbalanced by earthiness, citrus and mild warmth.
critics.summary: The page displays an expert score of 89 but does not explicitly state its scale.

notes: Producer source is a Volcán promotional site carrying Moët Hennessy USA attribution. It provides an overall profile rather than separate sensory stages. No numeric age statement was verified.

producer.summary: The producer describes its artisanal range as using prolonged oven cooking, concrete fermentation vessels and double distillation.

critics.nose: Cooked agave accompanied by vanilla, oak, caramel and restrained pepper.
critics.palate: Agave remains prominent alongside butterscotch, cinnamon-like spice, wood and fruit.
critics.summary: An approachable, balanced sipping tequila with restrained intensity. The review displays 88 without explicitly stating the scoring scale.

facts.mash_bill: Agave from the Tequila Valley; cooked in stone ovens, roller-milled and fermented in concrete vessels.
facts.cask: American white-oak bourbon barrels; stainless-steel pot distillation with a copper coil.

notes: The critic explicitly reviews Artesanal Suave Reposado at 40%, aged 11 months. Producer sensory fields remain empty: its own page supplies range-level production information. Japanese importer-operated brand notes were not treated as producer-authored notes.

producer.summary: The official brand partner describes a profile combining flowers, herbs and citrus after maturation in whiskey barrels.

critics.nose: Grilled citrus, pale chocolate, pastry and white pepper, with floral and herbal nuances.
critics.palate: Velvety and lively, relatively dry despite its fruit character, with cashew, caramel, cinnamon and almond-confection flavors.
critics.finish: Long, warming and layered, carrying nutty, caramelized and spiced flavors.
critics.summary: The panel praises the combination of mature complexity and a bright, mineral-agave character.

notes: Standard Reposado only; Single Barrel and Throwback releases were excluded. Official G4 partner page supplies the producer profile. Its aging text conflicts internally: introductory text says six months, while production details say three to six months in American-oak bourbon barrels; no single age was assigned.

producer.finish: A restrained impression of barrel maturation.
producer.summary: The producer emphasizes cooked-agave character with a gentle wood-influenced ending.

critics.nose: Peach and pear mingle with pine, dill and agave.
critics.palate: Rounded and slightly sweet, with apple-like fruit, vanilla, tropical fruit, citrus and warming spice.
critics.finish: Long and herbal, retaining agave, citrus and a lightly salty, peppery character.
critics.summary: A full, rounded reposado whose citrus and spice balance the sweeter fruit notes.

facts.mash_bill: 100% highland agave; brick-oven cooking. Combines tahona processing with fiber fermentation and roller-mill production.

notes: Producer notes are translated from Spanish and are not strength-specific. Critic explicitly identifies 40% and 80 proof; its tasting dates to 2011. Aging is a production duration in the review, despite its separate metadata saying no age statement.

critics.palate: Pepper leads, followed by a brief savory, meat-like impression.
critics.finish: Long, with ginger and cayenne warmth.
critics.summary: Despite its pale appearance, the reviewer finds substantial flavor and complexity.

facts.mash_bill: 100% Blue Weber agave from the Jalisco Highlands.

notes: Facts come from exclusive US importer Charbay. Its sensory quotations are explicitly attributed to critics and were not placed in producer fields. Wine Enthusiast reviews the 40%, eight-month expression; Difford's 38% bottling was excluded.

producer.summary: Mango-led fruit combines with peppery spice and earthy depth; the producer also identifies cocoa and dried-chile nuances.

critics.nose: Citrus, sweet agave and smoke with an earthy character.
critics.palate: Soft and creamy, repeating the aromatic flavors with an additional clay-like nuance.
critics.summary: The page displays an expert score of 90 without explicitly stating its scale.

facts.mash_bill: Espadín agave; electric milling. Palenqueros: Paciano Cruz Nolasco and Marcos Cruz Mendez.
facts.region: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico

notes: Standard Single Village Espadín expression at 47%; Vida and Azul were excluded. Producer sheet provides an overall descriptor list rather than separate sensory stages. Individual production batches are not identified by the critic.

producer.summary: Floral character, vanilla, fig, caramelized honey and lemon peel accompany minerality and an unusual fruit-driven funk.

critics.palate: Savory pepper and smoked-meat flavors, with spice, astringency and tart cranberry and currant fruit balanced by restrained smoke.
critics.finish: Delicate lemon zest and a creamy clay-like impression.
critics.summary: The review explicitly identifies 50% and distinguishes it from earlier 49% batches.

critics.nose: Grilled mint, berry dessert, orange, plum, leather and buttery smoked banana.
critics.palate: Vibrant and very dry, with layered fruit, nuts, savory impressions and ripe plantain.
critics.finish: Very long and warming, retaining complex fruit, roasted-nut and savory flavors.
critics.summary: The panel highlights exceptional complexity, including cocoa, smoky leather, citrus and roasted berries.

facts.mash_bill: Espadín agave, hand-milled with wooden bats and subjected to extended wild fermentation. Listed palenqueros: Florencio Carlos Sarmiento, Florencio Carlos Vasquez, Luis Carlos Vasquez and Luis Carlos Martinez.

notes: Used the producer's 50% sheet and critics explicitly reviewing 50%. The older producer sheet specifying 49% was excluded. Current producer descriptors are not separated into nose, palate and finish; exact batch identifiers were unavailable.
